Q1: The hazard profile for o-Xylene indicates several known hazards, primarily at Tier 1 (Globally Harmonized System). These include carcinogenicity, mutagenicity and reproductive hazards, acute and chronic environmental hazards, inhalation hazards, oral hazards, and organ and systemic hazards. Dermal and eye hazards are at Tier 2, reflecting an expanded understanding beyond GHS, while endocrine disruption hazards are classified as Tier 4, indicating insufficient data for assessment.
Q2: o-Xylene is classified on multiple 'Lists of Concern'. It is designated as a hazardous substance under the Clean Water Act, requiring reporting if discharged into navigable waters. Additionally, it is listed as a Hazardous Air Pollutant by the EPA under the Clean Air Act, signifying its regulation due to potential adverse effects on air quality.
Q3: o-Xylene is exceptionally well-characterized. With 36,000 literature references, it is significantly more studied than most chemicals in our dataset of fracking and petrochemical materials. Its precise molecular formula (C8H10) and classification as a 'Small Molecule' further confirm its well-defined nature, with only one hazard class (endocrine disruption) identified as data deficient.
